extracted.intended_audience: hospital quality measurement staff, hospital administrators, measure developers, and stakeholders participating in the CMS Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and proposed policy for measures, reporting, risk adjustment, and scoring used in the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program (including EDAC measures, birthing-friendly designation, and eCQM reporting requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: 30-day outcome timeframe for EDAC measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a 30-day outcome window for EDAC measures (consistent with existing measure specifications and aligned with condition-specific 30-day readmission measures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 30-day timeframe allows reflection of hospital discharge planning including follow-up, care coordination, and patient self-management education; maintains consistency with previously endorsed measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Medicare Advantage beneficiaries in EDAC cohort
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify EDAC measures to include Medicare Advantage beneficiaries in the measure cohort (in addition to Medicare Fee-For-Service).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed beginning with FY 2028 payment determination; measure developer considerations and empirical exploration of differences between Medicare Advantage and Fee-For-Service beneficiaries may be required (example: AMI EDAC endorsed with condition to explore such differences by the next maintenance cycle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance period length (2-year reporting) for modified EDAC measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce the performance period for specified EDAC measures from 3 years to 2 years, with public reporting using 24 months of prior data for the measurement period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal applies beginning with the July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2026 performance period associated with the FY 2028 payment determination; results publicly reported annually on Compare tool or successor website.

rubrics_metrics.name: EDAC data source and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate modified EDAC measures using administrative data from Medicare Fee-For-Service claims or Medicare Advantage encounters (or both).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals would not be required to report additional data; enrollment status obtained from the Medicare Enrollment Database; measures calculated and publicly reported annually using 24 months of prior data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment components for EDAC measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk-adjust EDAC measures for patient functional status (frailty indicator), patient-level demographics (age), and patient-level health status and clinical conditions (case-mix adjustment, comorbidities, severity of illness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure developer considered threats to validity during development/testing; model discrimination (c-statistic) and predictive ability should be examined to assess adequate adjustment and differentiation of excess days in acute care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical selection of risk variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Select risk variables for hospital-level case-mix adjustment empirically based on prevalence, correlation, and association with the outcome (combine index and pre-index codes accordingly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: STEMI identified as a risk adjustment variable for AMI EDAC while NSTEMI was not; selection should consider clinical severity and coding prevalence; developers should evaluate and document selection rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model performance evaluation (discrimination and predictive ability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate risk model performance using model discrimination (e.g., c-statistic) and predictive ability metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites AMI EDAC c-statistic of 0.68 and predictive ability of 1.4% to 10.1% as evidence of adequate discrimination for a readmission-type measure; developers should report such statistics and calibration testing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical update: use of individual ICD-10 codes for risk adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Update risk adjustment methodology to use individual ICD-10 codes instead of grouping codes via CMS HCC categories to improve condition-specific risk adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS has previously applied the same update to other measures (MORT-30-STK, COMP-HIP-KNEE); developers should document improvements in model performance and provide technical detail (see Table IX.C.4 referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure endorsement and maintenance process adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures should follow the Partnership for Quality Measurement/CBE endorsement and maintenance process and meet endorsement criteria for review cycles and maintenance schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Heart Failure EDAC and Pneumonia EDAC last endorsed Spring 2021 and planned for Fall 2027 maintenance; AMI EDAC endorsed with conditions in Spring 2025 (condition: empirically explore differences for Medicare Advantage when returning in Spring 2030).

rubrics_metrics.name: Birthing-Friendly Hospital Designation eligibility: Maternal Morbidity Structural attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals must positively attest to the Maternal Morbidity Structural measure (a two-part attestation regarding participation in perinatal QI collaboratives and implementation of patient safety practices) to be eligible for the Designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals respond 'yes', 'no', or 'not applicable'; positive attestation is a prerequisite for any tiered/expanded Designation and currently the sole criterion for the Designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of Cesarean Birth and Severe Obstetric Complications eCQMs into Designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Potentially expand the Designation criteria to include two maternal outcome eCQMs: Cesarean Birth eCQM and Severe Obstetric Complications eCQM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outcome measures are mandatory for hospitals in the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting and Medicare Promoting Interoperability Programs beginning with CY 2024; proposed inclusion would require hospitals to report on both to be eligible under the expanded methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cesarean Birth eCQM definition and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cesarean Birth eCQM measures proportion of cesarean deliveries among nulliparous term singleton vertex births; hospital-level score is a proportion for which lower is better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scores are not expected/desirable to approach zero because cesarean may be clinically warranted in emergencies; methodology report and further details available at referenced methodology link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severe Obstetric Complications eCQM definition and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk-standardized measure assessing severe maternal morbidity events and mortality during delivery hospitalizations (patients >=8 and <65 years; >=20 weeks' gestation) with two outcomes: any severe complications, and complications excluding transfusion-only events; reported as rates per 10,000 delivery hospitalizations where lower is better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiating outcomes that exclude transfusion-only events prioritizes higher-severity complications; methodology report referenced for full details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite scoring steps for expanded Birthing-Friendly Designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate the two maternal outcome measures into a composite score using specified preprocessing, weighting, aggregation, peer grouping, and clustering steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: (1) change score direction so higher = better; (2) log-transform non-normal-distributed scores and standardize using Z-scores; (3) multiply standardized scores by assigned weights (Cesarean Birth 45%; Severe Obstetric Complications outcomes: 18% for any, 37% for excluding transfusion-only); (4) sum weighted scores to generate composite; (5) group hospitals into delivery-volume peer groups; (6) apply k-means clustering within peer groups into three clusters representing levels of maternal care quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting rationale for composite maternal outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign differential weights to outcome measures to prioritize more outcome-related and higher-severity measures in the composite score (Cesarean Birth 45%; Severe Obstetric Complications combined 55% with split 18% and 37%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher weighting for Severe Obstetric Complications elevates attention to reducing maternal morbidity; greater weight assigned to the outcome excluding transfusion-only encounters because transfusion-only may represent lesser severity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer grouping by delivery volume for Designation scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Group hospitals into four peer groups by delivery volume during the performance period (<=500, 501–1000, 1001–2000, >2000 deliveries) to compare hospitals of similar scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer grouping supports fair comparisons; CMS solicits input on whether categories (e.g., <=500) are appropriate for small/rural hospitals, whether minimum birth thresholds (e.g., 25) should apply, and whether alternative variables (like Maternal Levels of Care) are suitable (noting lack of comprehensive public data on Maternal Levels of Care).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiered award and public display for Birthing-Friendly Designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Award Designation icons in a tiered manner based on cluster assignment within peer groups: cluster one = one icon (lowest performance), cluster two = two icons, cluster three = three icons (highest performance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shifts away from a binary label toward recognizing ranges of performance; positive attestation remains prerequisite; CMS requests feedback on presentation and interpretability on the Compare tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing and inclusion thresholds for maternal measures public reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For public reporting and inclusion in testing of the modified scoring methodology, hospitals must report on the measures and meet minimum count thresholds (example: 25 or more delivery hospitalizations during the measurement period aligns with public reporting threshold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary testing used hospitals that reported at least one maternal measure and, for composite testing, hospitals that reported on all three measures and had >=25 deliveries; zero-denominator declarations allow compliance when no patients meet denominator criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation topics for public comment on Designation changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Request feedback on scoring methodology, small/rural/safety-net hospital considerations, measure weighting, tiered awarding, peer grouping approaches and categories, minimum births per peer group, other peer grouping variables and data sources, and presentation/interpretability on the Compare tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will consider input for future rulemaking and methodology refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on eCQM reporting ramp-up and mandatory timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Progressively increase number of mandatory eCQMs, allowing hospitals time to self-select and implement new eCQMs; proposed policy to make certain eCQMs mandatory after defined self-selection periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal: Malnutrition Care Score eCQM mandatory beginning CY 2028/FY 2030; Hospital Harm eCQMs to become mandatory in the third year of reporting or after 2 years of self-selected reporting depending on timing (example: Falls with Injury and Postoperative Respiratory Failure mandatory CY 2028; Postoperative VTE mandatory CY 2030 after 2 years self-select). Newly adopted Hospital Harm eCQMs would become mandatory after 2 years of self-selected reporting in the future.

rubrics_metrics.name: eCQM submission file and successful submission criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable submissions for eCQMs include a QRDA Category I file with patients meeting initial patient population, a zero denominator declaration, or a case threshold exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to previously adopted QRDA Category I file format requirements and the Annual Update for technical specifications; zero denominator declaration allows hospitals with no relevant patients to meet reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: eCQM technical specifications and update schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: eCQM technical specifications are maintained in the CMS Annual Update (issued the year prior to the reporting period) and implementation guidance is posted on the eCQI Resource Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: For CY 2026 reporting/FY 2028 payment determination, hospitals will use the May 2025 Annual Update and any applicable addenda; hospitals must register and submit quality data as required by 42 CFR 412.140(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal rationale for making Hospital Harm eCQMs mandatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Making Hospital Harm eCQMs mandatory after reasonable self-selection periods standardizes safety data collection, advances digital measurement, and improves patient safety by creating a robust national dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS expects hospitals to have progressive experience with eCQM reporting (12 years by CY 2028) and contends that mandating after self-selected reporting will produce representative data and potentially replace claims-based measures (e.g., PSI 90 components).
